title: NovaAI - POC capacity & autoscale scoping
summary: POC scoping to define success criteria and capacity plan. Customer wants a 2-week pilot to validate throughput and p95 latency for a chat-like workload. Discussed reserved GPU sizing, burst strategy to shared pools, fallback to smaller model variants, and KV/prefix caching. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing and security docs, run a baseline benchmark with sample prompts, customer to provide traffic profile and SLOs.
next_steps: Jordan to send draft pricing + Dedicated capacity options by 2025-04-07
Priya to schedule benchmark run and share test harness and spreadsheet by 2025-04-06
NovaAI to share sample request traces and target SLO matrix by 2025-04-05
Schedule follow-up demo of Dedicated autoscale config week of 2025-04-14
action_items: Jordan: send pricing deck and Dedicated SKU options (due 2025-04-07)
Priya: run baseline perf on 4xA100 equiv and share results (due 2025-04-06)
Asha/Liam: provide 48h sample traces + target p95/p99 latency and token distribution (due 2025-04-05)
Ana: share SOC2 / ISO docs link and support contact (due 2025-04-06)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-03 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jordan Myers, Priya Patel, Ana Gomez (Redwood) -- Liam Chen, Asha Kapoor, Marco Ruiz, Sofia Tan (NovaAI)

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, scope the POC capacity needs, success criteria, and autoscale/burst options.
00:18 Liam (NovaAI): thanks Jordan, we appreciate it. quick context, we're building a chat assistant embedded in our product. current traffic is small but we need to validate economics and latency for launch.
00:32 Asha (NovaAI): yes, typical request size is around 400 tokens input, 200 tokens output on average, bursty during biz hours, maybe 200 rps peak on day one if pilot goes well.
00:45 Priya (Redwood SE): okay, that prompt footprint helps. just to verify, your 400/200 numbers are tokens or characters?
00:51 Asha (NovaAI): tokens, tokenized by our tokenizer. the distribution has a long tail — some prompts go up to 1200 tokens.
01:05 Jordan: cool. for success criteria, what are your SLOs? p95, p99, cost targets?
01:12 Liam: p95 under 600ms ideally, p99 under 1.5s. cost-per-1k-responses target around $X — we shared a rough number in the RFP but it's flexible.
01:26 Priya: p95 600ms is ambitious for 400+ tokens but doable with right GPU and batching configs. there will be tradeoffs: more reserved GPUs lower p95 and predict cost, burst to shared reduces cost but adds variability.
01:42 Marco (NovaAI SRE): also need private network options later, but for POC hosted is fine. we need audit logs and encryption in transit.
01:50 Ana (Redwood CSM): noted, we'll include SOC2 and kms integration docs.
01:57 Jordan: let's talk capacity. a baseline POC we typically recommend reserved capacity for predictable perf. for your shape, a starting point is 4x A100-class GPUs reserved with autoscale to burst to 8.
02:12 Asha: can you explain burst mechanics? are we paying for burst too?
02:18 Priya: yes — burst uses shared pool at a higher per-token rate. reserved capacity covers base throughput. burst engages when queue builds or latency thresholds trigger. billing is split: reserved commit + metered burst usage.
02:34 Liam: what's the fallback policy if burst isn't available? we can't have calls failing.
02:40 Priya: good point — we have two fallback strategies: 1) route to a cheaper/quantized model variant with slightly lower quality but lower latency; 2) degrade response length (truncate or shorten completions) while flagging for re-try. automatic fallback rules can be based on queue depth or p95 breaches.
02:58 Asha: any impact on tokenization or chat state? we use KV cache heavily for multi-turn.
03:05 Priya: KV cache persists across requests for pinned sessions on Dedicated. on shared burst, KV cache warmup is slower, so we recommend sticky routing for hot sessions to reserved nodes. that reduces cold-kv penalties.
03:22 Jordan: benchmarks — we propose Redwood runs a baseline with your sample traces. we'll run two configs: reserved-only 4x, reserved+burst to 8, and a smaller 2x experiment to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:36 Liam: timeline?
03:38 Jordan: week 1 (next week) run baseline perf and validate end-to-end. week 2 iterate on autoscale rules and run customer-driven scenarios, then a results review. end of week 2 we decide on commit size for Dedicated.
03:52 Sofia (PM): how long to turn up reserved capacity?
03:56 Priya: reserved nodes take about 24-48 hours to provision, we can pre-warm some model caches. burst capacity is immediate but may have slightly higher latency.
04:10 Marco: do you support GPU-type substitution? like 80GB vs 40GB A100, or H100?
04:16 Priya: yes, we have recommended SKUs by model. for large context the 80GB class gives better throughput. H100 offers better perf for new models but availability and cost differ. we'll include a perf matrix.
04:30 Liam: what are benchmark success thresholds for the POC?
04:34 Jordan: we'll align on these but propose p95 < 700ms on reserved-only with throughput >= 150 rps sustained, and end-to-end quality parity within X% of your baseline. also cost per 1k responses for reserve+burst within your target.
04:52 Asha: okay. curious about autoscale policy specifics — does Redwood support queue-based and latency-based scaling triggers?
04:58 Priya: yes both. queue-based scales on request backlog; latency-based uses p95 sliding window. we can combine with cooldowns and max burst caps.
05:12 Marco: how do you route traffic to ensure sticky sessions? we run multi-turn chat and need KV cache continuity.
05:18 Priya: we support session affinity by user_id or cookie. for POC we'll set sticky routing for hot sessions to reserved pool. fallback sessions can still be served but with warmup.
05:30 Jordan: risk areas — when burst is exhausted, we recommend a chain: 1) try model variant fallback, 2) shorten completions, 3) queue with a client-side retry policy; we'll provide guidance for client behavior.
05:45 Liam: metrics and dashboards during POC?
05:48 Ana: Redwood Console will provide per-route latency, token-level cost, KV hit rates, and autoscale events. we'll share a demo dashboard and the perf spreadsheet.
06:00 Sofia: is there an SLA for POC?
06:05 Jordan: POC is not SLA-backed, Dedicated commits come with SLAs. but we instrument monitoring and alerts.
06:12 Asha: for privacy, can we run POC on Private deployment?
06:16 Jordan: we can but setup is longer. for pilot we suggest Hosted/Dedicated mix; Private is an option for the next phase.
06:26 Liam: any suggested model quantization to save cost?
06:30 Priya: we can recommend per-workload quantization profiles: int8 or q4 variants to reduce memory and cost with modest quality loss. we'll include recommended profiles in the perf report.
06:46 Marco: what about model fallbacks compatibility, like switching from 16B -> 7B? will outputs change a lot?
06:52 Priya: outputs will differ; we advise running evals on representative prompts. Redwood Optimize can run automatic regressions to flag quality drops.
07:06 Jordan: ok wrap up — recap next steps: Jordan sends pricing + Dedicated options, Priya runs baseline, NovaAI shares traces and SLOs, Ana shares security docs. schedule follow-up for results review week of 2025-04-14.
07:22 Liam: that works, thanks all.
07:25 Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the benchmark spreadsheet and the console demo.
07:30 (call ends)
